title: Needs a more mature concept
body:
I downloaded it during a free trial, and I love the prioritise lists, the educational side of it and later, more of a community feel. 

However, the interface and over all look is very much aimed at children and young adults. 

I like that you get rewards, helps boost that dopamine, but as an adult, I don’t want the reward to be a new emoji icon or stars falling down when I tick something off the list. 

As I said, great for kids and young adults but it was way too immature for me. 

Have an adult option where the rewards are like a free one on one with a specialist for an amount of points to you’ve accumulated. Something that will really help adults coping with ADHD.
author: Shivvi M

title: SCAM!
body: THIS IS SO DISRESPECTFUL. I signed up for the trial, cancelled two days before the deadline and still 5 months later I am being incorrectly charged every month. I deleted the app and when I googled how to rectify this issue it has to be done “in App” well it does not recognise me as a previous user as my subscription SHOUID BE CANCELLED. Instead it tries to sig me up again with my bank details. I would like a refund for the last 5 months please, and to have no more debits from my account! This is marketed as a helpful tool for people with adhd, instead it preys on people like us and takes us for granted. DISGUSTING

title: Amazing
body:
I’ve been able to stick with this app over the many others I’ve tried previously without feeling like it is work to open it. 
I suspect it’s the engaging colours, the dopamine hit of watching confetti falling down the screen after completing a task, the fact that its very simple and intuitive to use and that you get rewards and move up levels like a game 🥳
Well done Numo. A week in (a to do list app record for me) and have happily used and relied upon it every day.

title: WILL CHARGE AFTER CANCELLING FREE TRIAL
body: For an app aiming to support people with ADHD it sure is sneaky that they’ll charge you even after you cancel the subscription before the end of the free trial period like we don’t have already have enough ADHD tax accumulated. App wasn’t for me so cancelled pretty much straight away and just saw a charge in my apple wallet even though it had expired. I’m sure the app could be useful for people and this isn’t to say don’t use it but I’m leaving this review as a warning and I don’t like companies that capitalise off peoples’ mental health then employ shady tactics. Some people don’t have $25 AUD to be duped out of so maybe fix your advertising.
